chapter: Working with Duke and final reflections
title: Mercer Ellington, Duke's estate and Duke's visit before his hospital stay
summary: Whaley thinks the money changed Mercer, that Mercer's book on his father was wrong, and that Duke visited him with $100 and steaks before hospital.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now what are your feelings about Mercer and what he's done with the band? This is for posterity and I think someone that was as close to the father and to the big man as you are and so many of us have these feelings, what do you think what went wrong? What happened to him?
I don't know, Mercer went crazy, I think; he went off his lid when he got all this money from Duke. You know, Duke had left around $200,000, see. Something like that.
Uh huh.
And it changed Mercer all over.
That isn't too much money, for a great man like Duke, considering what his royalties must be like -- $200,000 is not too much money.
No, but Mercer didn't have no money.
Uh huh.

See, and I always thought that I was Mercer's money, see, because when we was in Las Vegas, we shared a room, see. And he'd take my money and go and gamble it and then bring me back money, and you know, I thought I was really his buddy.
But it seems like things change. He wrote that book about his father.
Isn't that too bad? I don't have the book.
No, but Ruth told me about it.
What did Ruth say? Is she upset about it?
Oh yes, she said he shouldn't have wrote it. Somebody else was telling me about how he talked about his father.
Yeah ...

I said that man should never have been talking about him like that -- I thought Duke, when Duke told me he was going to the hospital, he came down my house, he give me $100 and bought some steaks in a pan, see, and he says he's going into the hospital, and I said, 'Where you going?' and he said, 'Up there to Columbia' and I said 'Don't go there.'
Had you lost your sight then?
Yeah.
And so he came by to see you and brought you $100 and some steaks, huh?
And some steaks, yeah. He always used to come -- when he came up to the barbers, he nearly always would come by and see me and say how you doing and all that.
Uh huh.
And I was closer to Duke than Mercer, see, because I used to almost room with him, you know?
Sure.
He'd have a room there and we would have a suite, and I'd have a room there with him and we would stay in the biggest hotels, and oh --
And so you think the memory of a great man like that has been sort of ...
Tarnished.
Yeah.
